transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-10-16
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Lucas Chen (Redwood SE), Arman Gupta (Product), Tom Rivera (Aurelia CTO), Priya Singh (Lead ML Eng), Jorge Alvarez (DevOps), Nina (PM)

--- Summary / Notes ---
(automated) Summary: demo of hosted conversational generation; focused on streaming, param tuning, retry/backoff, console traces and cost. Customer asks about PHI encryption and latency guarantees.

00:00 Maya (Redwood): okay thanks everyone for joining, we'll keep this to ~45 minutes, quick intros and then i'll do a quick show and tell of the hosted gen console and lucas will deep dive into streaming and retries.
00:18 Tom (Aurelia): hi all, i'm tom, we run the ML infra at Aurelia HealthTech. main goals are lower latency for triage assistant and strict PHI controls.
00:27 Priya: hey, priya here. curious how you handle long conversations and kv cache stuff, we have multi-turn notes.
00:40 Maya: great, quick agenda. 1) hosted api demo - console + traces 2) streaming behavior and params 3) retries and fallback patterns 4) q&a and next steps.
01:05 Lucas (Redwood): jumping in, i'll demo a live conversation from the console sandbox. note: streaming is chunked, you get partial tokens as they generate; we also surface per-token cost and latency in the trace.
01:23 (chatter)
01:35 Lucas: starting live run now... sending request with temperature 0.2, max_tokens 256, top_p default. watch the stream come in.
02:03 Lucas: so you see the partial tokens, sometimes you'll get a pause while kernels refill or batching coalesces, that's expected — couple seconds in high concurrency.
02:45 Jorge (Customer): can that pause be eliminated? our app needs sub-400ms on short replies.
02:54 Lucas: short replies are a different path — fastpath config: lower max_tokens, use shorter context, and pinned model variant optimized for latency. We can also tune batching windows in Dedicated, but on hosted we do dynamic batching with windowing heuristics.
03:20 Maya: to add, Optimize can recommend quantization/profile for your workload; console shows estimated tokens per second and cost impact.
03:55 Priya: about long conversation state — do you keep KV cache across turns or do we send full history?
04:08 Lucas: we support prefix/KV caching. by default the platform will cache recent KV where possible to avoid re-encoding full history; however, if you need strict auditability we can flush or pin by session id. small note: when caching across private deployment there are additional controls for data residency.
04:50 Tom: PHI — do you have KMS/HSM and SOC2 attestation?
05:01 Maya: yes, we have SOC 2, and for Private deployments we offer customer-managed KMS integration and optional on-prem. hosted can be configured with encryption-at-rest, but if you require customer KMS we recommend Private. we'll share security pack.
05:22 Tom: good. also curious about retry behavior — we see partial outputs sometimes when a connection drops.
05:30 Lucas: retries are three layers: client side idempotency + server side retry + model-fallback. best practice: implement idempotency keys for request de-dupe, use streaming-aware backoff, and also enable fallback to a lower-cost or smaller variant if the primary times out.
05:58 Lucas: for streaming resumptions we expose chunk cursors and an ephemeral session id you can replay against. note these are best-effort and may re-run some tokens if state isn't pinned.
06:25 Priya: can you show example backoff settings?
06:31 Lucas: sure — demoing policy: initial 200ms, exponential backoff x2, jitter, max 5 retries; for streaming we also cap cumulative retry time to preserve UX.
06:50 (typing / click sounds)
07:05 Lucas: showing console trace for a sample request: timeline shows token emit times, kernel switch, queue wait. you can filter by token cost and see per-route latency percentiles.
07:38 Nina (Customer): is there a way to get alerted on regressions for quality? we run evals against prompts.
07:45 Arman (Redwood): yes, Optimize ties evals to rollouts — you can upload prompt sets and get automatic regression alerts when a new model variant or quantization profile changes outputs beyond threshold.
08:10 Tom: what's the typical price delta between low-latency variant and high-quality variant?
08:17 Maya: depends on model/size — usually low-latency tuned variants reduce token latency but cost might be similar; Optimize projects unit cost differences in the console for chosen profiles. we'll send examples in the benchmark sheet.
08:45 Priya: any limits on streaming connections? we need persistent websockets for many concurrent clients.
08:52 Lucas: hosted has soft limits per account; for scaled persistent connections we recommend Dedicated or Private with dedicated capacity. hosted can handle many but you might hit per-account socket limits.
09:10 Jorge: and if we need region residency — EU, APAC?
09:18 Maya: we have multiple regions; for strict residency we offer Private or regional-hosted options. we'll note regions in the doc.
09:40 (pause)
10:02 Lucas: quick demo of changing temperature live: raising temperature to 0.8 increases diversity, you'll see tokens change pace; for deterministic flows we recommend temperature 0-0.2 and use sampling controls.
10:30 Maya: we also show console experiments — can run A/B rollouts between variants and track latency/cost and quality metrics in Optimize.
11:05 Priya: about auditing — do you log full payloads or only hashes?
11:12 Maya: by default we store traces and token-level timing and costs; payload retention is configurable per account, and Private deployments can enforce zero retention or customer-controlled retention. we'll share retention options and audit log screenshots.
11:40 Tom: ok good. can you run a simulated connection drop and show the recovery?
11:47 Lucas: yep doing that now — initiating streaming then killing the client mid-stream; you can see server logs mark session as interrupted and client retries with same idempotency key will either resume (if within session window) or return from fallback variant.
12:25 (noise)
12:40 Lucas: see the stream resumed but a small overlap of tokens occurred; that's expected without strict checkpointing — if you need exact at-most-once semantics we'd recommend blocking replay and using full-state rehydrate.
13:05 Priya: fine. so for our triage assistant — target is median 300ms for 32 token replies, 95th under 800ms. possible?
13:18 Lucas: on hosted maybe tight; with pinned low-latency variant or Dedicated you can reach those numbers. we'll propose a benchmark plan to validate.
13:35 Maya: next steps we'll share a small benchmark matrix and a sandbox account; if results look good we can propose a short pilot on Dedicated.
13:50 Tom: sounds good. two quick legal questions: contract lead time and data processing addendum?
14:00 Maya: typical lead time for small pilot is 2-3 weeks; DPA and SLAs are standard addenda — we'll loop in legal once we sign NDA.
14:18 (crosstalk)
14:35 Nina: one more — competitor comparison, are there any features that are unique?
14:42 Arman: we highlight production-first metrics, per-token cost visibility, built-in Optimize recommendations and unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private. others may offer raw endpoints but less observability or fewer rollout primitives.
15:05 (beat)
15:20 Maya: ok wrapping up, i'll recap.
15:25 Maya: Recap: 1) we'll send product + security deck 2) Lucas sends benchmark sheet and sample retry policy 3) customer to share 3 prompts and latency targets by 2025-10-23 4) schedule pilot kickoff week of 2025-10-27.
15:45 Tom: thanks all, that works.
16:00 End meeting.
